rows.label: Adjustment for some contraception being unwanted or unused (Sierra Leone)
rows.explainer: Guess - Higher for Nigeria than SL because i i) greater share of contraception provided are LARCs and ii) seem to be average lower frequency of visits per community, which could mean clients find it harder to get a LARC removed. But with a higher proportion of short-term methods in SL, there's also higher potential for some contraception provided to be unused. But given high proportion of LARCs provided in both programs, I'm guessing inability to remove a LARC when wanted is the main source of negative value

rows.label: Adjustment for within-org or external funging (Sierra Leone)
rows.explainer: Rough guess. The average funging adjustment across GW Top Charities is -15 to -20%, excl. New Incentives (-5%). We apply a larger adjustment for Sierra Leone because we think it's possible that implementers could continue supporting outreach teams indefinitely using unrestricted funding (meaning our funding could in fact be supporting less cost-effective uses of funds), but apply a smaller adjustment for the new outreach teams in Nigeria, because we do not know of a currently-operating program in Nigeria and we think it's reasonably unlikely that an implementer would have used other sources of funding to add new teams in the current environment of reduced funding for family planning in LMICs.

Cost-effectiveness after leverage and funging adjustments (multiples of GiveWell benchmark) (Sierra Leone)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
